issue_context.title: Socket.SendAsync and ReadOnlyMemory<byte>.Empty throws exception
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

Using `Socket.SendAsync` with `ReadOnlyMemory<byte>.Empty` was throwing a "Bad address" socket exception on Linux.

Broken:

```cs
await socket.SendAsync(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>.Empty, SocketFlags.None).ConfigureAwait(false);
```

Works:

```cs
await socket.SendAsync(Array.Empty<byte>(), SocketFlags.None).ConfigureAwait(false);
```

I only saw this error in a docker container so it might be specific to Linux.

### Configuration

Docker image `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:5.0`.

### Regression?

No

### Other information

```
      System.Net.Sockets.SocketException (14): Bad address
         at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.AwaitableSocketAsyncEventArgs.CreateException(SocketError error, Boolean forAsyncThrow)
         at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.AwaitableSocketAsyncEventArgs.SendAsync(Socket socket, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
         at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.SendAsync(ReadOnlyMemory`1 buffer, SocketFlags socketFlags, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
```

### Description Using `Socket.SendAsync` with `ReadOnlyMemory.Empty` was throwing a "Bad address" socket exception on Linux. Broken: ```cs await socket.SendAsync(ReadOnlyMemory.Empty, SocketFlags.None).ConfigureAwait(false); ``` Works: ```cs await socket.SendAsync(Array.Empty(), SocketFlags.None).ConfigureAwait(false); ``` I only saw this error in a docker container so it might be specific to Linux. ### Configuration Docker image `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:5.0`. ### Regression? No ### Other information ``` System.Net.Sockets.SocketException (14): Bad address at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.AwaitableSocketAsyncEventArgs.CreateException(SocketError error, Boolean forAsyncThrow) at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.AwaitableSocketAsyncEventArgs.SendAsync(Socket socket, CancellationToken cancellationToken) at System.Net.Sockets.Socket.SendAsync(ReadOnlyMemory`1 buffer, SocketFlags socketFlags, CancellationToken cancellationToken) ```
Author: JamesNK
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Net.Sockets`
Milestone: -

"Bad address" maps to EFAULT, and the man page for send documents:
```
       EFAULT An invalid user space address was specified for an
              argument.
```
I suspect what's happening is we're passing down 0 as the buffer address with `Memory<byte>.Empty`, and even though the length is 0, the syscall still doesn't like it.  This doesn't happen then with `Array.Empty<byte>()`, as that's actually backed by a zero-length managed array, which does have a non-0 address.

This is just a guess; I haven't confirmed.
cc: @geoffkizer

I suspect the same.

I'm deliberating where the fix should go. I'm thinking it's probably best to do this at the deepest layer to avoid any issues here, i.e. just before we call Send.

Note we already special-case count==0 for receives here:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8093c52a9a4abde623c1bf8b74334f11030847f2/src/libraries/System.Net.Sockets/src/System/Net/Sockets/SocketPal.Unix.cs#L739-L752
If we need to special-case count==0 for sends as well, ideally it'd be in the corresponding place for the write path.

- `(ReadOnlyMemory<byte>)Array.Empty<byte>()` (valid empty array, zero length)
- `new ReadOnlyMemory<byte>(new byte[1], 0, 0)` (valid non-empty array, zero length)

The non-memory-specific version of this will cover your second example. 

I'm not sure there's enough variation in the third example to make it worth adding?
Just wondering: what is the behavior that makes it worth running the same test 3 times on the same socket?
Nothing in particular; I was mimicking other tests that do similar stuff. I can remove if you think it's weird.
buffer.IsEmpty would work,  too. That wouldn't mean it was a null ref,  but it wouldn't hurt to sub in Array.Empty for an empty span even if it's not null.
